By John Smith, Technology Correspondent March 14, 2025 Technology

New Rust Release Improves Compile Times by 20%

The Rust programming language team has announced version 1.85, which brings significant improvements to compile times across the board.

According to the release notes, the team focused on incremental compilation optimizations and parallel code generation, resulting in a 20% reduction in build times for most projects.

Key Changes

  • Improved incremental compilation cache hit rates
  • Parallel code generation enabled by default
  • New cargo check optimizations for large workspaces
  • Better linker integration on macOS and Linux

"We've been working on these improvements for over a year," said Rust team lead in a blog post. "The feedback from the community has been overwhelmingly positive during the beta period."

Industry Response

Several major companies using Rust in production have reported positive results. Dropbox reported a 25% reduction in CI build times, while Cloudflare noted improved developer experience for their edge computing team.

"This release makes Rust significantly more approachable for larger projects. The compile time has been a common pain point, and this addresses it head-on."

— CTO of a Fortune 500 company

Looking Ahead

The Rust team is already working on the next set of improvements, including experimental support for Cranelift code generation, which could bring even faster debug builds.

The release is available now through rustup. Developers can update by running rustup update stable.
